topic: Prioritize one device's speed on a shared home wifi network
core_question: What router feature lets you give one device (like a gaming console) priority bandwidth over others on the network?
answer_summary: Log into the router settings and turn on Quality of Service (QoS), then set the specific device as a priority so it gets more bandwidth than the others.
persona: dramatic and exasperated; using casual slang

messages.content: Yo my gaming console is getting totally destroyed by lag when my roommates are streaming and stuff. Like the wifi is so slow for me when they're on it. Is there a way to make my console get like more of the speed?

Okay so you want your console to get priority on the network when everyone else is using it—smart thinking? Have you ever dug into your router's settings, like actually logged into the admin panel, and checked what options are available there for managing how the internet gets distributed?

Yeah there actually is something most routers have—but first, can you get the password to log into your router's admin panel, and once you're in there, do you see any sections that mention traffic, management, or something about controlling how bandwidth flows to different devices?
